title: Chicken-wing contrast and shirt-fold drill

context.format: Short annotated visual tutorial with multilingual description
context.style: Red/green contrast and tactile setup close-up

coverage.transcript_kind: Persistent on-screen title; creator description read separately; no reliable spoken coaching
coverage.audio_transcription_note: Forced-English and auto-language ASR each returned a short non-coaching fragment. Preserve attempts without treating them as instruction.
coverage.visual_review_method: 12 overview and 31 detail frames across four portrait sheets plus one native-size shirt close-up, all inspected. Includes red/green change, shirt setup and delivery sequence. Sampled review, not continuous playback.
limitations: Interpretation of shirt contact comes from visual demonstration, not spoken procedure.
Edited views are not a controlled before/after comparison.
No exact impact timing, arm angles or pressure measurements.

cases.title: Use a gathered shirt fold as feedback for lead-arm connection
cases.coaching_finding: Creator targets left armpit opening associated with chicken wing. The clip stages a red/green comparison rather than diagnosing a named student.
cases.coach_reasoning: Post links the opening armpit to the unwanted pattern. Visual interpretation: gathered shirt supplies a contact feel for bringing lead upper arm closer through delivery. Further cause, force and eligibility explanation are absent.

intervention.drill: Gather a fold of shirt near left chest into left armpit, lower the arm against it, and rehearse the shown swing.
intervention.cue: Feel the shirt contact through delivery.
intervention.cue_origin: Concise model phrasing of the demonstrated task; not a spoken quote.
intervention.limits: No exact hold/release phase is given. Do not infer permanent clamping throughout the swing or a straight-elbow requirement at every phase.

applicability: A corresponding unwanted lead-arm separation pattern established in the golfer, with benefit from this contact rehearsal.
Requires a separate check that the arm pattern is an actionable priority rather than a compensation or functional variation.
unknowns: Cause of the golfer's pattern, ball flight and physical-screen context.
Precise fabric retention/release timing, contact force and practice dose.
Measured lead-arm change and transfer to ordinary swings.
cases.observed_result: Source shows staged contrast, shirt setup, rehearsal/shot footage and full finishes. No instrumented or longitudinal outcome.

selection.coaching_focus: Use one tactile cue for lead-arm connection
selection.policy_origin: User one-focus constraint; concise cue is a proposed presentation of the visual task.
selection.reassess: Proposed check: remove fabric constraint and compare delivery, comfortable finish and actual strike. The source supplies no controlled transfer test.

limits: Categorical source illustration, not calibrated movement measurement.

source_ambiguities.issue: The visual drill gathers shirt fabric, but the source does not specify exact release timing or retained pressure. Retain this gap rather than turning it into a permanent-clamp rule.
English post text is available alongside Korean/Japanese/Chinese. No model translation is needed for the stated target; audio fragment is not coaching evidence.

cross_source_links.relation: Related tactile connection idea with different release detail
cross_source_links.explanation: Ruffels explicitly lets the band release after delivery for a full finish. Hong shows shirt contact and a finish but supplies no precise release instruction; do not fill that gap with permanent clamping.
Ruffels uses upper-arm connection for control during speed work. Hong targets an illustrated chicken-wing pattern. Similar contact language does not prove the same cause or prescribe the same amount.

annotation_opportunities: Preserve source red/green labels alongside exact frames and mark them as source judgments.
Show the shirt-gathering close-up to explain the physical task.
Label proposed cue separately from verbatim source text.
excluded_material: Independent diagnosis of the demonstrator's natural swing.
Claim of improved distance, strike or scores.
Invented cloth retention timing, force percentage or universal elbow angle.

independent_validation.reason: Visual tutorial with minimal text; no diagnosis, calibrated outcome or stated release timing.
